decisions.reason: The supplier Statement separates the supplied-Spin associated construction from its assertion for any graded Hermitian Clifford module. Proof 3.1 allows overlap Spin lifts with a sign cocycle and explicitly does not assert a global multiplicity bundle; conjugation cancels the signs, and 4.1 patches the supertrace even when no global spinor bundle exists. Dimension zero is checked in 5.1. Thus the cited relative interface has no global Spin-lift prerequisite.

The supplied action, connection and contraction define data without choice. The final sentence attributes formal symmetry and global well-definedness to a lemma whose interface assumes Countable Choice, without mentioning that qualification. This is a nonfatal attribution/assumption omission, not a failure of the local contraction: inserted the exact Countable Choice qualifier, dependency and axiom metadata, preserving every defining equation and later domain restriction.

The divergence supplier explicitly requires positive dimension, whereas the lemma includes dimension zero. The zero-dimensional contraction is the zero operator, so its symmetry needs no divergence theorem. Added this direct branch before the positive-dimensional divergence argument, and corrected F3 to state n>=1; the frame-change contraction and the linear-first Hermitian sign calculation remain valid. This is a nonfatal omitted elementary boundary case, with no Statement change.

The Sobolev definition explicitly assumes Countable Choice as well as the Fourier suppliers. The original last step incorrectly confined its use to F2. Corrected A1 and step 3.1 to include F3 and the L2 subsequence argument; made the n=1 power unambiguous as |xi|^(1/2). Independently checked the multiplier domain, density of range, finite radial integral integral r dr, and divergent inverse integral integral dr/r for every n>=1. No mathematical conclusion or Statement changed.

F1 cites the geometric-module definition, which explicitly fixes Cl_C(T*M,-g) and the negative polarized relation. The universal plus-Q Clifford construction permits arbitrary quadratic forms: take Q(xi)=-g^{-1}(xi,xi) and polarize (xi+eta)^2. There is no opposite-sign premise. Checked the normal-frame expansion, [c_a c_b,c_k]=2(delta_ak c_b-delta_bk c_a), curvature commutant, and Bianchi/scalar contraction giving scal/4. No item edit is needed.

Formal symmetry of D is used in the energy identity, symmetry of DB, distributional resolvent testing and adjoint-domain argument, while the direct citation named only the defining data. Added the proved well-definedness/symmetry supplier to deps and F4 and cited it at each use, carrying its Countable Choice via full AC. This is a nonfatal missing explicit dependency: the formal-symmetry hypothesis and cited Lichnerowicz chain already made the analytic reasoning valid. Checked B:L2->H2, DB:L2->H1, the test identity u=DB(Du)+lambda Bu, graph-norm density and exact adjoint domain. Statement unchanged.

The referenced oriented bundle definition is topological and the supplied Euclidean metric need only be continuous. For the trivial oriented line over R with metric e^(2|x|), Gram-Schmidt of the constant frame gives e^(-|x|), which is not differentiable at zero. Thus the original unconditional smoothness assertion is false. Replaced it by continuity for the given topological data, with smoothness retained when the base, bundle and metric are smooth. The SO reduction, covering, rank range and continuous equivariant Spin-lift interface are preserved.

The needed central two-sheeted covering is proved by thm-real-pin-spin-topological-double-covers, already in the defining Spin-lift chain; its explicit logarithm section has smooth power series on smaller matrix balls. Added the covering theorem directly and separated its covering conclusion from the analytic smoothness calculation s(A)=exp(b(log A)), yielding translated smooth inverse branches. Checked smoothing of the actual supplied lift, finite Clifford averaging, connection gluing, local matrix-algebra factorization, sign-twisted overlap conjugacy and relative supertrace patching. The relative argument uses only trivial local Spin lifts. Statement unchanged; this is a nonfatal citation omission with the actual supplier available.
